newsitem.title: USA: Apple CFO says Q1 profit "too close to call".
newsitem.headline: Apple CFO says Q1 profit "too close to call".

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Chief Financial Officer Fred Anderson said the prospects for making profits in the first quarter of the company's fiscal 1997 were "too close to call".

Speaking with reporters in a conference call, Anderson repeated comments made to analysts earlier, that the company expects revenues to be relatively flat from its September quarter and gross margins to continue at or above 20 percent.
But he also said higher levels of consumer advertising in the current quarter, which is typically the year's heaviest selling season, can push operating expenses slightly higher.
"When you add all of that up, it's too close to call because we had a slight profit this quarter," he said.

Apple reported earnings per share of $0.20 for its fourth fiscal quarter to September 27, 1996, compared with $0.48 in the year-ago period. Excluding a gain, Apple would have earned $0.06 a share, or $8.0 million.

Wall Street analysts had expected Apple to post a loss of $0.30 a share, according to mean estimates compiled this week by First Call. The range of estimates was from a loss of $0.50 a share to breakeven.
